title: Ping Pong
summary: A classic pong-style game built in Unreal Engine to learn 2D input, ball physics and UI.
author: Solaras Light

title: Road Crossing
summary: An arcade-style road crossing game in Unreal Engine featuring grid-based movement, obstacles, collectibles and a scoring system.
author: Solaras Light

title: HTTP Server from Scratch (Java)
summary: A CodeCrafters challenge solution: an HTTP/1.1 server built from scratch in Java with request parsing, routing, persistent connections, gzip compression and file read/write endpoints.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: HTTP Server from Scratch (JavaScript)
summary: The same CodeCrafters HTTP/1.1 server challenge implemented in JavaScript (Node.js): request parsing, routing, keep-alive connections, gzip compression and file endpoints.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: Portfolio Website
summary: This site. A personal portfolio built with Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS, covering my IAM and full-stack work along with this roadmap.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: Solaras Light Portfolio
summary: A game development portfolio for Solaras Light.
author: Solaras Light

title: Canyon Salvo
summary: A turn-based missile duel built with libGDX. Each turn both sides place a missile launcher and a flare dispenser, then fire at once, and the enemy learns your habits. Runs on desktop, in the browser and on Android.
author: Solaras Light

title: TN5250 Emulator
summary: A modern IBM i (AS/400) 5250 terminal emulator built from scratch in Java 17. The protocol engine (Telnet negotiation, 5250 data stream parsing, EBCDIC conversion) is fully independent of the UI, with two front ends on top: a JavaFX desktop client and a Spring Boot browser client.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: OAuth 2.0 Server From Scratch
summary: A fully spec-compliant Authorization Server in Spring Boot, built without the Spring Authorization Server abstraction so that every grant type and token behavior is implemented by hand.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: Untitled Endless Driving Game
summary: An endless driving game with a cyber style, built with Unreal Engine and targeting Android.
author: Solaras Light

title: Untitled Mailing Framework
summary: A Java mailing framework to manage sending mail from Java applications.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: Polyglot IAM Suite
summary: One Keycloak authorization server in front of three independently written resource servers — Spring Boot (Java), FastAPI (Python) and Express.js (Node) — each enforcing the same JWT validation and RBAC rules through its own idiomatic security stack.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: Zero-Downtime Legacy Migration Utility
summary: Migrates thousands of users from an old database or a legacy Okta instance into Keycloak using a lazy (just-in-time) migration strategy, so users see no service disruption or forced password resets on day one.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: SSO Hub — Keycloak Identity Broker
summary: Federates three identity sources — Okta (corporate employees), a SAML 2.0 IdP and Google (customer/social login) — behind one Keycloak realm, with a Spring Boot API that normalizes every provider's claims into one internal identity shape. Covers the simpler two-IdP Okta + Keycloak employee/customer bridge as a base case along the way.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: The CI/CD IAM Automation Pipeline
summary: Manages identity configuration entirely as code, so Dev, Staging and Prod environments deploy deterministically without manual changes in the admin UI.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: Untitled Racing Game
summary: A racing game in the spirit of SkyRoads and Nitronic Rush.
author: Solaras Light

title: Microservice Mesh Security & Token Exchange
summary: Secures an ecosystem of Spring Boot microservices with the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern, keeping raw JWT access tokens out of browser storage to minimize security vulnerabilities.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa

title: Game Engine Auth Toolkit
summary: Implements the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Flow and PKCE natively inside Unreal Engine 5, Unity and Godot, all authenticated against a real Keycloak server.
author: Santhosh Laguduwa
